transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luca Romero (Redwood Solutions), Samir Rao (CTO - Lighthouse), Erin Blake (Platform), Priya Singh (Security), Tom Wu (DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh we'll do a 45 to 60 minute walk-through of the console controls for keying and rate zoning. is that timing still good?
[00:06] Samir (Lighthouse CTO): yes that's fine, we blocked an hour. a lot to cover so appreciate it.
[00:10] Maya (Redwood SE): quick intro, i'm maya, i work on infra optimizations and the routing side, i'll show the console and then we can jump into the pilot/bench plan.
[00:16] Erin (Platform): thanks, we mostly want to see how to translate our per-customer quotas to your org/project keys model, and how to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[00:23] Jordan: perfect. just so we know context — can you give a quick overview of your current stack and traffic patterns?
[00:29] Tom (DevOps): sure. we run a multi-tenant service, nginx front end, internal job queue for embedding/preproc, and we currently proxy calls to an external LLM provider. typical steady rps per tenant is 2-5 rps, with big tenants spiking to 60-90 rps for short bursts.
[00:42] Samir: and our SLAs are 100ms p50-ish for small prompts, p95 we accept up to 600ms, but cost is a strong constraint — we want predictable bills.
[00:51] Maya: ok that helps. in Redwood we recommend an org -> project key hierarchy: org keys for company-wide governance, per-project keys for product teams or tenants. keys let you slice quotas, concurrency, and routing. we'll demo that.
[01:05] [01:05] Jordan: quick question — are you considering hosted API or dedicated capacity? or do you need private VPC immediately?
[01:11] Priya (Security): security-first for us, we prefer VPC or private deployment for PII workloads, but for non-sensitive features hosted could be ok during pilot. KMS integration is a must.
[01:19] Jordan: understood. we support customer-managed KMS in Private, and for Hosted we encrypt at rest with our keys, plus enterprise customers can enable a bring-your-own-key path — we'll detail that in the security doc.
[01:28] Maya: demo start — console home. i'll share my screen. [screen share noises] this is the org overview. you can see org-level quotas and a top-level traffic heatmap.
[01:40] Maya: if you click Keys -> Projects, you can create a new project key and set a per-minute and concurrency limit. here's a sample: project key "lighthouse-prod" with 600 rps burst and a concurrency cap of 20 per key. the UI also surfaces which model variants are pinned.
[01:57] Erin: that concurrency cap — is that per connection or per token stream?
[02:01] Maya: it's per-request concurrency. for streaming tokens we count active sessions, so if you have long-lived streams it's accounted for. we also have token-based quotas for monthly spend.
[02:12] Tom: how do you handle bursts from a single tenant? like if a tenant suddenly spikes to 5k rps?
[02:16] Maya: two layers — burst buckets (leaky-bucket style) and fairshare lanes. we do graceful backpressure at the gateway and can route overflow to a lower-cost model or queue with retry-after headers. for very large spikes we recommend dedicated capacity or can policy route to a fallback model to keep critical paths online.
[02:32] Samir: who gets priority? we have paying customers and internal traffic — can you do priority lanes?
[02:37] Maya: yes, you can tag keys with priority levels. higher-priority keys get reserved lanes and can preempt fairshare when you enable reserved capacity. that shows in the routing policy editor here.
[02:47] Jordan: i'll also mention sticky routing. if you want the same tenant to keep a session on the same pool for latency reasons we support affinity based on project key or session cookie.
[02:56] Priya: audit logs and SSO — can we see per-key usage, and is that in the audit trail?
[03:01] Luca (Redwood): yep. all API calls are logged with key, model, latency, and tokens. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or to our retention archive; retention windows are configurable on dedicated/private.
[03:10] Priya: and SAML/SSO?
[03:12] Jordan: supported — SAML, OIDC, RBAC at org and project granularity. we'll send a security pack.
[03:17] [03:17] Erin: about quotas — i want per-tenant monthly token budget and also a per-second throttle in bursts, is that possible with a single project key?
[03:24] Maya: yes. each project key can have multiple quota dimensions: token/month, requests/minute, concurrent sessions. you can attach policies that say "when token budget hits 90% -> restrict to X rps".
[03:33] Tom: curious about KV cache and prefix cache — we rely on cached completions a lot to reduce cost. how does Redwood cache interact with multi-tenant keys?
[03:41] Maya: we have prefix caching and KV cache per logical keyspace. you can either use org-level shared cache or per-project partitioned cache to avoid cross-tenant leakage. note that shared cache improves hit-rate but needs stricter privacy guarantees. the UI shows cache hit/miss statistics per key.
[03:56] Samir: can you show the routing policy editor? we want a policy that favors low-latency model for paying customers and uses cheaper quantized model for exploratory queries.
[04:04] Maya: sure — clicking policies. here's a policy: route by key priority -> if priority high and latency SLO <200ms route to low-latency pool; else route to quantized variant. you can also set capacity thresholds at the pool level, auto-burst to dedicated pools, or failover to fallback endpoints.
[04:21] Erin: any way to test these policies without impacting production?
[04:24] Jordan: yes, we have canary rollout and traffic shadowing. you can run a policy in "dry-run" to see simulated hits and impact on token spend.
[04:31] [04:31] Maya: switching to the Optimize tab — here's our recommendation engine. it looks at your traffic profiles and suggests batch sizes, quantization, and pinning models for latency vs cost. for example, it suggests batching small prompts into 8-concat for one of your tenants.
[04:44] Priya: is the optimize engine on-prem? or does it send telemetry?
[04:47] Luca: by default recommendations are generated in our control plane. on Private you can opt into a local analyzer, and telemetry can be limited to aggregated metrics only; we can exclude PII traces. we'll include options in the security doc.
[04:58] Samir: performance question — if we run a pilot on hosted can we get realistic p95 numbers?
[05:03] Maya: yes, we can run a short benchmark using your sample traces. typical approach: you send a trace file with timestamps, prompt sizes, and concurrency distribution, we run a 10k-call replay across the same model variants and return p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[05:17] Tom: how long does that take?
[05:18] Maya: usually 24-72 hours depending on queue. we can prioritize for pilots.
[05:22] Erin: any gotchas around token accounting when using fallback models for cost-savings? we need to keep accurate billing per tenant.
[05:29] Jordan: billing is per request/token and can be attributed to project key. when fallback happens to a cheaper model it's still recorded against the same key. you can see cost per key in the billing view.
[05:37] [05:37] Samir: latency vs cost tradeoffs — do you have a built-in cost simulator we can plug our traffic into?
[05:42] Luca: yes, we have a cost simulation tool in the console that estimates monthly spend based on model mix and token rates; you can run scenarios with different quantization and batching settings.
[05:51] Priya: security/regulatory — do you have SOC2 reports and an option for data residency in eu?
[05:55] Jordan: we have SOC2 Type II, ISO in progress, and Private deployments support region pinning for data residency. we'll attach the compliance pack in follow-up.
[06:05] Erin: ok, let's talk pilot scope — we want to validate two things: (1) policy-based fairshare prevents noisy-neighbor impact; (2) cost per 1M tokens with recommended optimizations.
[06:15] Jordan: recommended pilot steps: ingest sample traces (Erin), Redwood runs 10k-call benchmark (Maya), we share latency/cost report and fine tune policies, then run a short canary in hosted with traffic shadowing, then consider dedicated pool if needed.
[06:28] Tom: can we do the initial benchmark without sharing raw prompts? we can send anonymized traces.
[06:32] Maya: yes anonymized traces are fine; for stricter privacy we accept token lengths and timing only.
[06:37] Samir: ok good. on the legal side, procurement will ask for indemnity and SLAs for dedicated. can you share sample MSA?
[06:43] Jordan: yes i'll include sample MSA + pricing in the follow-up.
[06:47] [06:47] Erin: question about rollout automation — can you auto-adjust quotas by time of day? we have global customers in EDT and APAC windows.
[06:53] Maya: you can schedule quota windows and set hourly scaling policies. autoscaler can increase burst capacity during pre-defined windows and revert.
[06:59] Priya: last security nit — for KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:02] Luca: yes on Private we support HSM integrations and you can rotate keys per your policy.
[07:06] Jordan: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:09] Jordan: recap: we showed org/project keys, quota dimensions, routing policies, cache partitioning, optimize recommendations, and pilot plan. agreed next steps are Jordan sends pricing/MSA, Maya runs benchmark with anonymized traces, Erin shares traces, Priya outlines compliance questions.
[07:23] Samir: sounds good. thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[07:26] Tom: thanks, i'll coordinate the traces.
[07:28] Priya: i'll send compliance items.
[07:30] Jordan: great — i'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff and send the security pack.
